subject: Renewal: Blue Harbor - pricing pause & phased commit transition
messages:
From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@blueharbor.co>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement <procurement@blueharbor.co>, Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@blueharbor.co>
Date: 2027-09-22T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Hi Tessa,

Quick note as we start renewal planning — our engineering team is migrating a major workload to a new inference pipeline in Q4 which will change our per-token profile. We expect a usage dip for ~6–8 weeks during the migration window.

Because of that timing risk, procurement is requesting a short price hold through the migration (a 60-day pause at current rates) so we don’t get re-priced mid-migration. After the pause we’re open to a revised commit structure (possible staircase commits for the next 12 months).

Can your team outline options we could present to our CFO (credits vs. price hold vs. phased commit)? We want something that preserves predictability for both sides.

Thanks —
Sophie
Sophie Lemaire
Head of AI Platforms, Blue Harbor
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@blueharbor.co>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-22T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the context and the heads-up about the migration. We can definitely propose a few structured options that balance your need for a short-term rate freeze with Redwood's capacity economics. I put our internal team on this thread to model options quickly.

High-level options we can turn into a simple one-pager for your CFO:
- Short price hold (60 days) + prorated credits to reconcile actual consumption after migration
- Phased commit staircase: lower initial commit for Q4, step-up in months 3/6/12; built-in burst pool for migration spikes
- Credit buffer: prepaid credits that act as a usage floor (protects you from price shocks; unused credits convert to discounted overage or roll into next quarter)

I’ll attach a draft proposal today — Dylan, Marcus: please model 3 variants (hold+credit, staircase, credit buffer) with rough $/token and effective blended rate for year 1.

Sophie — will schedule a 30-min call later today if that works.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Sophie Lemaire <sophie@blueharbor.co>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-23T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Sophie / Tessa —

Attached is a preliminary table (see attached PDF) and a short narrative. Quick summary of the modeling:

Option A — 60-day price hold + reconciliation credits
- Hold at existing rates for 60 days starting at renewal
- After migration, we reconcile against actual usage; if usage < forecast, we issue credits to reach the forecasted commit dollar amount
- Effective impact to Redwood: temporary margin compression during hold; moderate operational reconciliation work

Option B — Phased commit staircase
- Year 1 commit starts at 60% of target, steps to 85% at month 4, and 100% at month 9
- Built-in 20% burst pool billed at a reduced overage rate
- Better for us operationally; more predictable multi-quarter revenue

Option C — Prepaid credit buffer
- Blue Harbor prepays a credit block covering expected migration shortfall; unused portion converts at a 10% discount to next quarter
- Least operational churn for Redwood; shifts cash to Redwood upfront

I included a blended $/token for each variant in the PDF. Marcus: note margin and capacity notes.

Attachment: BlueHarbor_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal + cost table)

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@blueharbor.co>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement <procurement@blueharbor.co>
Date: 2027-09-24T07:46:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Tessa / Dylan —

Thanks for the speedy reply and the PDF. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance: 
- Procurement likes Option B (staircase commit) but wants a formal price hold window for the first 60 days to avoid any mid-migration rate changes.
- Finance prefers Option C (credit buffer) because it reduces forecast volatility on their P&L.

Can you produce a hybrid: a short price hold (60 days) + a staircase commit where the staircase is slightly delayed and includes a small upfront credit buffer to cover the migration dip? If you can show the blended effective rate and a short legal clause for the hold, we can take to our CFO next week.

Andrea
Andrea Rossi
VP, Procurement — Blue Harbor
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@blueharbor.co>, Sophie Lemaire <sophie@blueharbor.co>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-24T12:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Andrea —

Yes — we can do that hybrid. I uploaded a redline that captures: 1) explicit 60-day price hold clause (no rate changes for covered SKUs during the hold); 2) staircase commit schedule with step dates and volumes; 3) a small credit buffer (equivalent to ~8% of annual commit) applied at T0 and reconciled at month 3.

Key bullets for your CFO:
- Predictability: 60-day hold prevents mid-migration churn on pricing
- Alignment: staircase lets Blue Harbor scale commit with product adoption while protecting Redwood with step ramps
- Protection: prepaid credit absorbs migration shortfall and converts per negotiated rules

I attached the redline for legal. If that looks OK we can generate a final SOW + DocuSign package and route through your procurement contact.

Attachments: BH-Commit-Redline_20270924.docx

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: procurement <procurement@blueharbor.co>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@blueharbor.co>, Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@blueharbor.co>
Date: 2027-09-28T15:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + temporary price hold request

Tessa / Team —

The CFO reviewed the hybrid and gave preliminary approval pending two small changes: 1) clarify the reconciliation timing (final reconciliation at month 4, not month 3); 2) include a maximum cap on the credit conversion to avoid open-ended liabilities.

If you can update the redline with those two items, we can execute before EOW. Also please include the DocuSign packet link when you send the final.

Thanks —
Blue Harbor Procurement
procurement@blueharbor.co
